newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Wash Mutual says deal to proceed.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Wash Mutual says deal to proceed.

text.p: Great Western Financial Corp's proposed merger with Washington Mutual Inc should proceed as planned even if hostile suitor H.F. Ahmanson and Co raises the ante, Washington Mutual Chairman Kerry Killinger said on Wednesday.
"The market's already voting in our favor, and momentum is clearly in support of us," said Killinger. "We expect to get the shareholder vote June 13 and close soon thereafter."
Both bidders are proposing stock swaps, but a surge in Washington Mutual's share price has wiped out Ahmanson's premium, leading some analysts to believe Ahmanson may sweeten its bid again.

Ahmanson declined to say if it would raise its bid. But Killinger said during an interview Ahmanson had limited success after raising its bid in March, and if it tried again, the result would likely be the same.
"There has already been an adjustment on the hostile offer on this one, and the markets have now spoken and said that even with an increase, they are favoring our transaction," he said.
"I think it is highly likely that any additional increase that someone might do would be fully disciplined by the capital markets because of the questionable dilutive nature it would have," he said.

Great Western agreed to merge with Washington Mutual in early March in an effort to thwart Ahmanson's hostile bid. Ahmanson responded by boosting its offer and is now offering to swap up to 1.2 of its shares for each Great Western share.
Washington Mutual is offering to swap 0.9 of a share for each Great Western share.
Both bids were worth about $6.8 billion Wednesday, with Ahmanson's bid at $49.06 a share and Washington Mutual's at $50.04 a share.
Killinger said he was confident the shareholder vote would occur on June 13, despite a court hearing May 30 on a request by Ahmanson to delay the proceedings.

According to court papers made available to Reuters on Wednesday, Vice Chancellor Jack Jacobs of the Delaware Chancery Court approved a request by Washington Mutual to be an intervenor at the hearing.
"Our attorneys say that they are very confident that the June 13 votes will proceed," said Killinger.
Killinger is credited with building Washington Mutual largely through acquisitions, including the recent purchase of California-based American Savings Bank.

He said he expected Washington Mutual may be ready for additional acquisitions in California as soon as six months after the Great Western deal closed. He expects that transaction to close shortly after the June 13 vote.

"As soon as we are comfortable that operating plans are going along well with Great Western, we'd look at additional expansion in California," he said. He declined to name any potential acquisition targets.
